abstract: We consider a non-convex constrained optimization problem, where the objective function is weakly convex and the constraint function is either convex or weakly convex. To solve this problem, we consider the classical switching subgradient method, which is an intuitive and easily implementable first-order method whose oracle complexity was only known for convex problems. This paper provides the first analysis on the oracle complexity of the switching subgradient method for finding a nearly stationary point of non-convex problems. Our results are derived separately for convex and weakly convex constraints. Compared to existing approaches, especially the double-loop methods, the switching gradient method can be applied to non-smooth problems and achieves the same complexity using only a single loop, which saves the effort on tuning the number of inner iterations.

summary.idea: The method switches between objective improvement and constraint handling within one loop. The paper analyzes it for weakly convex objectives with either convex or weakly convex constraint functions.
summary.limitations: The guarantee concerns near-stationarity under the specified weak-convexity assumptions, not a global solution. The abstract does not provide numerical experiments or wall-clock comparisons demonstrating the practical savings.
summary.problem: Constrained nonconvex optimization can require complex nested procedures, especially when objectives or constraints have sharp corners. Simpler switching subgradient methods lacked comparable nonconvex complexity guarantees.
summary.results: The analysis establishes oracle complexity for reaching a nearly stationary point, matching the compared nested approaches while accommodating nonsmooth functions and avoiding inner-loop iteration tuning.
summary.tldr: A simple single-loop method gains convergence guarantees for an important class of nonsmooth constrained problems.

title: Oracle Complexity of Single-Loop Switching Subgradient Methods for Non-Smooth Weakly Convex Functional Constrained Optimization
